display_name: Terroir Al Limit Les Tosses, Catalunya
raw_content:
{
  "hook": "Les Tosses is a 1.1 ha north-facing Carignan parcel at 750 m on the slate-rich llicorella slope above Torroja; Dominik Huber ferments it 100% whole-cluster, ages it eight months in 2,500 L foudre, and the 2022 just hit 13% alc while clocking 97 points from the only critic who has seen it. That combination—high-altitude Carignan on broken slate, bottled at Burgundian weight—doesn’t exist anywhere else in Spain.",
  "wine_summary": "Terroir al Limit was founded in 2004 by Huber and South-African winemaker Eben Sadie to prove Priorat could do freshness, not just power. They farm biodynamically, pick at 12–13% potential alcohol, and never exceed 30% new oak; the result is a set of site-specific reds that read like northern Rhône Syrah wearing Catalan boots. Les Tosses, bottled as Vi de Vila de Torroja, is their Carignan flagship: vines planted 1910 on costers (stone terraces) so steep that mules still deliver the fruit. The wine delivers black cherry, dried rosemary, and a stony ferric snap that tastes like licking a hot slate after rain—exactly what llicorella soil does when yields are held to 15 hl/ha.",
  "terroir_expression": "Broken slate (llicorella) is the key: sheets of black and copper-coloured schist fracture vertically, forcing vine roots to dive 6–8 m for water. That hydraulic stress concentrates flavour while the slate’s high iron and magnesium content shows up as a bloody, ferrous note on the mid-palate. At 750 m the parcel sits just above the summer inversion layer, so nights drop to 14°C even in August, locking acidity into Carignan’s naturally late cycle and stretching harvest into mid-October. North exposure gives only morning sun, so skins stay thin, tannins remain fine, and alcohol stays below 13.5%—a profile impossible on the southern amphitheatre where most Priorat prestige sits.",
  "vinification_summary": "100% whole-cluster carbonic maceration lasts 21 days in open 2,000 L stainless vats; spontaneous fermentation finishes at 24°C, then the wine is pressed directly into neutral 2,500 L Austrian foudre for eight months. No punching down, no sulfur until bottling at 20 ppm total. The technique tames Carignan’s hard seed tannins, letting whole berries ferment inside the skins and yielding a perfumed, almost Beaujolais nose while still delivering Priorat mineral depth—essentially Cru Fleurie on slate steroids.",
  "food_pairing": [
    "Nashville hot chicken sandwich—acidity and fine tannin cut the cayenne oil, while schist minerality mirrors the saline pickle brine.",
    "Grilled lamb skewers with rosemary and smoked paprika—herbal echo of garrigue, smoke links to the whole-cluster stem spice.",
    "Catalan escudella (meat & chickpea stew) poured tableside—the ferric note marries morcilla blood sausage and the broth’s iron richness.",
    "Roasted beet and goat-cheese salad with hazelnut vinaigrette—earth-sweet beet mirrors wine’s iron tone, acid brightens the dressing.",
    "Aged Manchego curado plus Marcona almonds—tannin grips the sheep-milk fat, slate streak keeps the finish clean."
  ],
  "comparable_wines": [
    "Clos Mogador Manyetes 2020 — same llicorella, higher elevation Carignan but sees 16 months oak, giving more tannic heft.",
    "Domaine de Courcel Bourgogne Pinot Noir ‘Rugiens’ — iron-rich clay/silex gives similar bloody minerality, though lighter body.",
    "Lopez de Heredia Viña Tondonia Reserva — traditional Rioja Carignan blend with comparable whole-cluster herb lift and long aging potential."
  ],
  "style_profile": "Medium-bodied dry red with slate-driven tannins and whole-cluster herb lift",
  "cellar_recommendation": "Drink 2025-2035; 12°C single-zone fridge, lay bottles flat; no decant needed before 2027, 30-min air after if you open younger.",
  "value_assessment": "€75-€90 retail in Europe, $110-$130 US; sits beside Château de Saint-Cosme Côte-Rôtie at the same money but offers 100-year vines and lower alcohol. Worth it if you want Priorat without the syrup.",
  "market_position": "You’ll find it by-the-glass at Barcelona’s Gresca and Madrid’s Sala de Despiece, not at Costco. Buyers are somms who need a ‘Burgundy’ option for Grenache-heavy lists, plus collectors tracking every Terroir al Limit cuvée.",
  "insider_take": "Skip the 2018—heatwave flattened aromatics; 2022 is the freshest since 2014 and will shut down soon, so stash a six-pack if you like iron-tinged Carignan at 13%. Most people still think Priorat has to be 15% and opaque; this bottle is the counter-proof, but it will never sway the Parker crowd.",

parsed.hook: Les Tosses is a 1.1 ha north-facing Carignan parcel at 750 m on the slate-rich llicorella slope above Torroja; Dominik Huber ferments it 100% whole-cluster, ages it eight months in 2,500 L foudre, and the 2022 just hit 13% alc while clocking 97 points from the only critic who has seen it. That combination—high-altitude Carignan on broken slate, bottled at Burgundian weight—doesn’t exist anywhere else in Spain.
parsed.wine_summary: Terroir al Limit was founded in 2004 by Huber and South-African winemaker Eben Sadie to prove Priorat could do freshness, not just power. They farm biodynamically, pick at 12–13% potential alcohol, and never exceed 30% new oak; the result is a set of site-specific reds that read like northern Rhône Syrah wearing Catalan boots. Les Tosses, bottled as Vi de Vila de Torroja, is their Carignan flagship: vines planted 1910 on costers (stone terraces) so steep that mules still deliver the fruit. The wine delivers black cherry, dried rosemary, and a stony ferric snap that tastes like licking a hot slate after rain—exactly what llicorella soil does when yields are held to 15 hl/ha.
parsed.terroir_expression: Broken slate (llicorella) is the key: sheets of black and copper-coloured schist fracture vertically, forcing vine roots to dive 6–8 m for water. That hydraulic stress concentrates flavour while the slate’s high iron and magnesium content shows up as a bloody, ferrous note on the mid-palate. At 750 m the parcel sits just above the summer inversion layer, so nights drop to 14°C even in August, locking acidity into Carignan’s naturally late cycle and stretching harvest into mid-October. North exposure gives only morning sun, so skins stay thin, tannins remain fine, and alcohol stays below 13.5%—a profile impossible on the southern amphitheatre where most Priorat prestige sits.
parsed.vinification_summary: 100% whole-cluster carbonic maceration lasts 21 days in open 2,000 L stainless vats; spontaneous fermentation finishes at 24°C, then the wine is pressed directly into neutral 2,500 L Austrian foudre for eight months. No punching down, no sulfur until bottling at 20 ppm total. The technique tames Carignan’s hard seed tannins, letting whole berries ferment inside the skins and yielding a perfumed, almost Beaujolais nose while still delivering Priorat mineral depth—essentially Cru Fleurie on slate steroids.
food_pairing: Nashville hot chicken sandwich—acidity and fine tannin cut the cayenne oil, while schist minerality mirrors the saline pickle brine.
Grilled lamb skewers with rosemary and smoked paprika—herbal echo of garrigue, smoke links to the whole-cluster stem spice.
Catalan escudella (meat & chickpea stew) poured tableside—the ferric note marries morcilla blood sausage and the broth’s iron richness.
Roasted beet and goat-cheese salad with hazelnut vinaigrette—earth-sweet beet mirrors wine’s iron tone, acid brightens the dressing.
Aged Manchego curado plus Marcona almonds—tannin grips the sheep-milk fat, slate streak keeps the finish clean.
comparable_wines: Clos Mogador Manyetes 2020 — same llicorella, higher elevation Carignan but sees 16 months oak, giving more tannic heft.
Domaine de Courcel Bourgogne Pinot Noir ‘Rugiens’ — iron-rich clay/silex gives similar bloody minerality, though lighter body.
Lopez de Heredia Viña Tondonia Reserva — traditional Rioja Carignan blend with comparable whole-cluster herb lift and long aging potential.
parsed.style_profile: Medium-bodied dry red with slate-driven tannins and whole-cluster herb lift
parsed.cellar_recommendation: Drink 2025-2035; 12°C single-zone fridge, lay bottles flat; no decant needed before 2027, 30-min air after if you open younger.
parsed.value_assessment: €75-€90 retail in Europe, $110-$130 US; sits beside Château de Saint-Cosme Côte-Rôtie at the same money but offers 100-year vines and lower alcohol. Worth it if you want Priorat without the syrup.
parsed.market_position: You’ll find it by-the-glass at Barcelona’s Gresca and Madrid’s Sala de Despiece, not at Costco. Buyers are somms who need a ‘Burgundy’ option for Grenache-heavy lists, plus collectors tracking every Terroir al Limit cuvée.
parsed.insider_take: Skip the 2018—heatwave flattened aromatics; 2022 is the freshest since 2014 and will shut down soon, so stash a six-pack if you like iron-tinged Carignan at 13%. Most people still think Priorat has to be 15% and opaque; this bottle is the counter-proof, but it will never sway the Parker crowd.
